title: objectql plugin: a package's script-bodied action is not bound when its name is shipped by another holder — judge "artifact-shipped" by owner key, not by name
body:
domain:server#4 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgWRcTEB3toGxnWvuvX

Out-of-scope should-fix of #32751 (PR #32987, triage review 6841909747). Not a regression: the name-only filter `isArtifactShippedAction` in `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` came with 4f5b79164 (2026-07-05), before #32741, so script-bodied actions in this composition never ran on a booted kernel. #32987 narrows its FROM→TO to "its declaration is served" and leaves the handler binding to this card. Graded p2 by the epic seat's rule (regression ⇒ p1, else p2); queued, not dispatched.

Filing gate: ② an epic-seat routing. class: b · type: Defect · Suggested-grade: p2 · lane: `domain:server`.

## What happens

On a booted kernel, the objectql plugin skips binding a script-bodied action when its name is shipped by an artifact, checking the name only. When two holders share a name, the holder whose declaration is served gets no handler, so its route reaches the action but nothing runs.

## Do

- Judge "artifact-shipped" by the owner key of the action (package + object), not by the bare name, so each holder binds its own handler.
- Pin on a booted kernel: two holders of one name, each runs its own body; one ablation per pin.
- Declare the moved answer (`Clause-②` per AGENTS.md step 3).

Reader who acts: `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (`isArtifactShippedAction`).
